record.paper_title: Solutions to four open problems on quorum colorings of graphs
record.original_question: If a graph G satisfies ψ_q(G) = 1, must its diameter diam(G) be at most 2?

evidence.quote: Hence, we deduce that lim ℓ→+∞ diam(Gℓ) = +∞, which answers Questions 3 and 4 in negative.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple connected graph. For a vertex v∈V, let N[v] denote the closed neighborhood of v (i.e., v together with its neighbors). A partition π={V_1,V_2,…,V_k} of V into nonempty color classes is called a quorum coloring of G if for every vertex v∈V, at least half of the vertices of N[v] lie in the same class as v; that is, |N[v]∩V_i| ≥ |N[v]|/2 whenever v∈V_i. Define ψ_q(G) to be the maximum number of classes k in any quorum coloring of G. Let diam(G) denote the diameter of G.

Question: Does ψ_q(G)=1 imply diam(G) ≤ 2? Equivalently, must every connected graph admitting no nontrivial quorum coloring have diameter at most 2, or does there exist a family of connected graphs G_ℓ with ψ_q(G_ℓ)=1 and diam(G_ℓ)→∞?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was resolved in the negative: there exists a sequence of connected graphs G_ℓ with ψ_q(G_ℓ)=1 whose diameters tend to infinity, so ψ_q(G)=1 does not imply diam(G)≤2.

status_evidence.claim: A construction yields connected graphs with ψ_q=1 but unbounded diameter, refuting the diameter-≤2 conjecture.
